chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Three (things): one who recognizes these would not leave them – cutting the hair, and rolling up of the clothes, and copulating with the slave-girls.

key_terms.تَشْمِيرُ الثِّيَابِ: Rolling up or girding the garments

ai.seo_question: What are the three practices a believer should not abandon according to this hadith from Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) linking personal grooming and social status to spiritual awareness. The 'cutting of hair' is interpreted by Shia scholars as maintaining the Sunnah of trimming (qass) rather than full shaving, while 'rolling up garments' (tashmir) signifies humility and readiness for worship. The inclusion of 'marrying slave-girls' reflects the historical legal context of concubinage as a permissible social institution for the knowledgeable believer.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Moamar Bin Khallad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Three (things), one who recognises these would not leave them – Cutting the hair, and rolling up of the clothes, and copulating with the slave-girls’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one comes to know of three things he will not ignore them. They are clipping hairs, rolling up clothes and going to bed with slave-girls.”’
